entry.title: package-trends 0.1.0
entry.content:
Minor Changes

  • Column charts, a fixed domain so two charts can be compared, point marks, settable up/down colours, and analyse() for writing about a series programmatically.

    Adds a styles object for weight, display and spacing; numberFormat and percentFormat taking Intl.NumberFormat options; interactive for pointer and keyboard inspection; aggregate: "month"; between() for an explicit date range; a band chart of each period's low, mean and high; CSS lengths for width and height so a chart can scale with its text; curve for smooth, stepped or straight lines; strokeDasharray, pathProps and fillPattern for patterned charts; and svgProps for anything else the <svg> should carry.

    Also repairs the zeros npm reports for days it has no data for. Taken literally they understate the mean by a quarter and invert the weekday profile; they are now interpolated, and listed in gapDays.

  • Compare several packages at once, from a new /compare entry: <PackageComparison> as an overlaid chart or a row each, compare() and indexSeries() in the core, and fetchMany so a page asks for each distinct name only once.

    scale="indexed" restates each series against its own start, which is the only honest way to put packages of very different sizes on one chart.

  • First release. npm download trends as a sparkline, a line of text or a KPI block, with a framework-agnostic core and a React entry. Pass data from a server-side fetchDownloads to render without a request per visitor.
